screening_decisions.reason: This is a double-blind controlled study comparing carbamazepine and diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) as monotherapy in 38 patients with psychomotor epilepsy (focal onset seizures). Although it uses a crossover design, it directly compares the two drugs of interest as monotherapy in the relevant seizure type.

This study randomly assigned 43 newly diagnosed epileptic patients to receive either phenytoin or carbamazepine monotherapy. While the primary outcome measured is cognitive function rather than seizure control, it is a randomized comparison of the two drugs of interest as monotherapy. Being conservative, this should be included for potential IPD extraction.

This is a systematic review/meta-analysis that synthesizes individual patient data from 20 randomised trials. It is not an original randomised controlled trial itself, but rather a secondary analysis of existing trial data.

This is a prospective randomised pragmatic trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs (including phenytoin and carbamazepine) as monotherapy in 243 adult patients with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures with or without secondary generalisation. This meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper discussing principles of equivalence trial design. It is not a clinical trial comparing carbamazepine or phenytoin monotherapy.
This is a prospective observational cohort study of 525 patients with newly diagnosed epilepsy. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing specific antiepileptic drugs as monotherapy.
This is a review article discussing principles of AED therapy. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This study examines cognitive function in 87 patients across three groups (starting AED, withdrawing AED, switching from phenytoin to carbamazepine). There is no indication of randomisation, and the primary outcome is cognitive function rather than seizure control.
This is an animal study conducted in rats examining phenytoin-folate interactions. It is not a human randomised controlled trial.

This is a long-term, prospective, randomised, pragmatic trial comparing four standard antiepileptic drugs (including phenytoin and carbamazepine) as monotherapy in 167 children aged 3-16 years with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures with or without secondary generalisation. This meets all selection criteria.
This is an epidemiological survey estimating incidence and prevalence of 12 neurologic disorders in the United States. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This study evaluated carbamazepine in 45 institutionalized patients whose seizures were NOT controlled by combinations of currently available antiepileptic drugs. This is not a monotherapy comparison trial - patients were already on combination therapy.
This is an epidemiological study determining the incidence of epilepsy in HMO populations. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This is a 10-center, double-blind randomised trial comparing four antiepileptic drugs (including carbamazepine and phenytoin) as monotherapy in 622 adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. This meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article discussing diagnostic accuracy and case ascertainment methods in epilepsy epidemiology. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

This study examines the effect of phenytoin or carbamazepine on somatosensory evoked potentials in 45 patients with focal epilepsy. There is no clear indication of randomisation, and the primary outcome is electrophysiological measurements rather than seizure control or treatment failure.
This is a population-based prospective incidence study of epilepsy in Iceland. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing antiepileptic drugs.

This is a methodological paper describing methods for extracting hazard ratios from survival curves in meta-analyses. It mentions a systematic review of carbamazepine vs valproate (not phenytoin) as an illustration, but is not an original RCT.
This is a meta-analysis estimating the global burden of epilepsy. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing antiepileptic drugs.
This is a position paper presenting the updated ILAE classification of epilepsies. It is not a randomised controlled trial.

Double-blind RCT comparing carbamazepine vs diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) as monotherapy ('given without other medication') in patients with temporal lobe/partial seizures (focal onset). Meets all selection criteria.

Review article about phenytoin use in dermatology/cutaneous conditions. Not a clinical trial, does not compare carbamazepine vs phenytoin, and focuses on dermatological applications rather than epilepsy treatment.

Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin as 'single anticonvulsants' (monotherapy) in 47 patients with focal and major generalized seizures. Directly meets all selection criteria.

RCT with 64 children with epilepsy randomly assigned to carbamazepine, phenytoin, or valproate monotherapy. While valproate is also included and the primary outcome is cognitive, the study does compare CBZ vs PHT monotherapy in the target population. Include conservatively.
In vitro mechanistic study using cell lines (human embryonic kidney cells, rat cortical neurons). Not a clinical trial in humans with epilepsy.
Study focuses on zonisamide pharmacokinetics and drug interactions. Does not compare carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
Preclinical laboratory study using mouse neuroblastoma cells. Not a clinical trial in humans.
Methodological guideline paper for reporting systematic reviews. Not a clinical trial.
Multi-drug comparison trial but does NOT include carbamazepine. Only phenytoin (diphenylhydantoin) is among the tested drugs, with no CBZ vs PHT comparison possible.
Secondary analysis/network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. This is a synthesis of existing trial data rather than an original trial.
Observational case series of 15 children who experienced seizure exacerbation on carbamazepine. Not a randomized controlled trial, no comparison with phenytoin.
Systematic review focused on teratogenic outcomes in pregnancy. Not a primary RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT for seizure outcomes.
Case series of 5 children with aberrant reactions to carbamazepine. Not a randomized controlled trial, no comparison with phenytoin.
Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin as 'sole treatment' (monotherapy) in 45 patients with partial and generalized epilepsy. Meets all selection criteria.
Clinical Q&A/letter format discussing teratogenic risks. Not a randomized controlled trial.

Prospective RCT with 55 patients randomly assigned to carbamazepine, phenytoin, or phenobarbitone monotherapy. While the primary outcome is cognitive effects and phenobarbitone is also included, the study does compare CBZ vs PHT monotherapy in the target population. Include conservatively.
Study examining trace element biomarkers (zinc, copper) in patients on various AEDs. Not primarily comparing CBZ vs PHT for seizure outcomes; outcome measure is biochemical markers.

Described as a 'double-blind' controlled trial of carbamazepine. Abstract does not clearly specify the comparator drug(s). Could potentially compare CBZ vs PHT. Include conservatively pending full-text review.

Prospective trials of phenytoin and carbamazepine in untreated patients with grand mal or partial seizures. Abstract does not explicitly confirm randomization between the two drugs (could be separate cohorts). Include conservatively pending full-text review.
Prospective observational study examining teratogenic outcomes in children exposed in utero. Explicitly states it is an 'observational study', not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a double-blind crossover study comparing carbamazepine (CBZ) with diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin/DPH) in epileptic patients. The study design is a controlled comparison of the two drugs in monotherapy, which meets the selection criteria for RCTs comparing CBZ vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is a systematic review about neurodevelopmental outcomes in children exposed to AEDs in pregnancy. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a methodological paper discussing individual patient data meta-analysis approaches for AED monotherapy trials. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is a prospective registry study about malformation risks from AED exposure in pregnancy. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a methodological paper about measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is a study about outcome reporting bias in systematic reviews. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is an epidemiological study about the incidence of epilepsy and unprovoked seizures in Rochester, Minnesota. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is a case series about absence seizures developing in adults on carbamazepine therapy. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is a preclinical study examining the effects of phenytoin and carbamazepine on Na+ channels in mammalian cell lines. It is not a clinical RCT in patients with epilepsy.
This is an observational study about the natural history of epileptic seizures in Denmark. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.

This is a double-blind crossover study comparing carbamazepine with phenytoin (Dilantin) in 40 adult epileptics. The study evaluates psychotropic effects of both drugs in a randomized design, meeting the selection criteria for RCTs comparing CBZ vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is a Cochrane review comparing phenobarbitone versus phenytoin monotherapy. It does not compare carbamazepine vs phenytoin, and it is a review rather than a primary RCT.

This is a record linkage study about the risk of serious cutaneous disorders after initiation of phenytoin, carbamazepine, or valproate. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a prospective community-based cohort study about factors predicting prognosis of epilepsy. It is not a RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.

This is a randomized study comparing phenytoin (DPH) and carbamazepine (CBZ) in 40 newly diagnosed, drug-naive adult epileptic patients. Patients were randomized into DPH and CBZ groups, meeting the selection criteria for RCTs comparing CBZ vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is a RCT comparing phenobarbital versus phenytoin for childhood epilepsy in rural India. It does not compare carbamazepine vs phenytoin, so it does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about extracting summary statistics for meta-analysis of survival endpoints. It is not a primary RCT comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
